answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 33% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned so that nobody profits from it. Because the meadow forfeiture is applied at exit, the sonnet ledger totals each burn, and the yarrow audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 132 aliases as a result destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 7 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
